articles.title: All passengers accounted for after tanker hits cruise ship, New Orleans mayor says
articles.summary: The mayor of New Orleans said on Friday evening that all of the more than 100 passengers aboard a cruise ship docked at the Port of New Orleans on the Mississippi River had been accounted for after a large asphalt tanker crashed into it, causing it to sink. Mayor Helena Moreno said at a news conference that the collision between the American Heritage cruise ship — a riverboat-style ship — and a tanker called the Atlantic Asphalt occurred around 12:30 p.m. after the tanker “lost control.” She said that passengers immediately began disembarking, but as they did so, the cruise ship capsized. Reports suggest that at least a dozen people fell into the water. New Orleans police, Harbor Police, firefighters and other boats on the river helped rescue them, Moreno said, adding that 32 passengers were hospitalized with noncritical injuries. “At this moment … we have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi,” she said. “And that is a credit to the first responders.” Bystander footage from the scene showed the white, riverboat-style cruise ship slowly tipping onto its side following the collision as passengers waited on the deck. American Cruise Lines, which operates the American Heritage, shared a message on social media saying that it was “ deeply concerned ” for everyone involved. “We are in close coordination with the U.S. Coast Guard and local authorities. Guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved. We will share more information as it becomes available.” This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/live/all-passengers-accounted-for-after-tanker-collides-with-cruise-ship-in-new-orleans-mayor-says-223554822.html

articles.title: DHS says no national security threat is behind FAA's nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights in the United States until further notice, "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." This means that planes currently in the air may land, but those on the ground may not take off. U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters Friday evening that there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat is behind the communications outage affecting flights. "There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for their loved ones," Mullin said. "This is not another 9/11," he added. "This is a telecommunications outage; this is much different." Mullin said it would "take some time" to resolve the issue and that flights already in the air are being handled on a "case-by-case" basis. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote in a post on X , "The @FAAnews issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them." As of 6 p.m. ET, there were over 10,000 flights delayed and over 1,700 canceled within, into or out of the U.S., according to FlightAware.com , a live flight tracker website. There were more than 30,000 departures and arrivals scheduled for the remainder of the day, according to flight tracking app Flighty, the New York Times reported . Airlines for America, an industry trade organization representing major U.S. airlines, wrote in a post on X , "Safety is always our top priority." It added that it's in communication with the Department of Transportation and the FAA. The association encouraged travelers to be in touch with their airline carrier for "real-time updates." Sen. Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois and a ranking member of an aviation subcommittee, called for an investigation into the nationwide ground stop. "The safety of our skies is built on redundancies," she wrote on X in response to Duffy's update. "Whatever led to the nationwide ground stop will warrant a thorough and complete investigation. As Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, I'll be demanding answers from the FAA." The cause of Friday's widespread communication issue is still unclear. "Do we know what has caused it yet?" Mullin said. "No, we're going to go through it. But I'm not going to make assumptions." Microsoft said that its own global outage — from which it is still recovering — did not appear to be a factor. Earlier this week, the FAA announced the nationwide rollout of a new $875 million artificial intelligence tool to help air-traffic controllers avoid delays. Called SMART — short for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories — it was made by an AI company called ASI and had previously been in use at Washington, D.C., airports since late September. On social media, ASI said "the current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC." A Yahoo reporter who is currently on the tarmac on a United Airlines flight waiting to depart from Los Angeles International Airport passed along updates from the cabin. She said her pilot said that "what happened was a communications outage that started in Kansas City Center, which is responsible for the airspace above the middle of America, and it spread nationwide." She also said she received an update from United Airlines, which said, "Air traffic control is limiting the number of planes allowed to land and depart each hour in Los Angeles, affecting several flights. We're monitoring the situation closely to get you to your destination as soon as possible." Around 6 p.m. ET, she said her flight “going over the Pacific” was finally “pushing back” from the gate. The New York Times has reported that “some international flights from the United States have been allowed to depart amid the ground stop.” Nationwide ground stops are pretty rare. The last time such an event occurred was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Before then, a nationwide ground stop was issued following the September 11, 2001, attacks. articles.title: White House correspondents' dinner shooting suspect faces new terrorism charge
articles.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, the man accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in April, is facing a new charge of terrorism, according to the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia. Allen was already charged with attempting to kill Trump and three other charges, but the new charge unsealed in a superseding indictment on Thursday adds a terrorism charge with not much detail. Dana Verkouteren - PHOTO: Cole Allen, the suspect in the shooting incident in Washington at the annual White House Correspondents' Association Dinner appears before Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh in US District Court in Washington, April 27, 2027. He has pleaded not guilty to the previous charges, including attempted assassination of the president, assault on a federal law enforcement officer with a deadly weapon, transportation of a firearm and ammunition over state lines with the intent to commit a felony and discharge of a firearm during a crime of violence. He has not yet entered a plea under the new charge. The armed 31-year-old was tackled by law enforcement on the night of April 25 after rushing through a security checkpoint at the hotel, where thousands of journalists as well as Trump and members of his Cabinet were gathered for the annual event, according to prosecutors. Footage shows White House correspondents' dinner suspect 'casing' hotel, US attorney says A Secret Service officer was shot and injured before Allen was subdued by agents, officials said. In May, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeannie Pirro said there is "no doubt" that Allen shot a uniformed Secret Service officer. Andrew Harnik/Gettyimages - PHOTO: Armed Secret Service agents stands on stage during a shooting incident at the annual White House Correspondents Association Dinner at the Washington Hilton on April 25, 2026 in Washington, DC. "The grand jury agreed that there was probable cause to believe that it was Cole Allen's weapon that hit the Secret Service agent," she told ABC News' chief justice correspondent Pierre Thomas. Allen allegedly wrote that administration officials were his targets, according to a criminal complaint. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of life in prison. articles.title: Lauren Boebert loses House seat to Democratic challenger in Colorado
articles.summary: In what had been considered Colorado's most Republican-leaning congressional district, incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert has been defeated by Democrat Eileen Laubacher. The Associated Press called the race on Friday afternoon. Laubacher received 48.8% of the vote (187,488 votes) to Boebert's 47.9% (184,047 votes), with 99% of the vote counted. Douglas Mangeris, a libertarian, received 3.3%, or 12,720 votes, per AP. Boebert, an outspoken gun rights activist, has served in Congress since 2021 and is considered one of President Trump's staunchest allies on Capitol Hill. Laubacher is a retired U.S. Navy rear admiral who was deployed in Afghanistan. She also served on the National Security Council under President Joe Biden. Laubacher's victory adds Colorado's 4th District to the more than 40 Republican-held districts that have flipped to Democrats this midterm cycle, including two others in Colorado. In an interview with NewsNation on Thursday, Boebert blamed her impending loss on "so many different variables" that plagued Republicans across the country, including gas prices, the war in Iran and Congress's failure to address corruption in the U.S. political system. She also argued that she and other members of the right wing House Freedom Caucus "weren't heard" when they called for Congress to take action on a variety of issues that voters care about, including government surveillance and "fair elections." The result is indicative of the remarkable swing toward Democrats that took place in historically safe Republican districts across the country. Boebert, who relocated from Colorado's more-purple 3rd District in 2023, won by more than 11 percentage points the last time she was on the ballot. Who is Eileen Laubacher? Laubacher served 34 years in the U.S. Navy, working in a variety of intelligence and command positions, before retiring in 2024. Her father also spent his career in the Navy, reaching the rank of vice admiral. Her grandfather served as a Navy combat diver during World War II. Laubacher spent significant periods of her Navy career abroad, including a deployment to Afghanistan in 2009 and service in a senior role at the U.S. Embassy in India. Though she said she had frequently told people in her life that she would "never run for office," Laubacher opted to enter the race for Boebert's seat because she believed residents of Colorado's 4th District deserved "serious and honest representation" in Congress. Laubacher had reportedly been a Republican throughout much of her life before registering as a Democrat in late 2025. Her decision to switch parties, she said, was driven by her view that the Republican Party had become "nearly unrecognizable" to her. Laubacher's recent party swap became the subject of a lawsuit during the Democratic primary, with one of the other Democrats in the race attempting to prevent her from qualifying for the ballot. That effort failed, and Laubacher later secured the Democratic nomination. In terms of policy, Laubacher is firmly within the moderate wing of the Democratic Party. She supports strong immigration enforcement, tax cuts for the middle class and reducing the national debt. She placed a heavy emphasis on affordability throughout her campaign, including calling on President Trump to repeal tariffs that raise consumer prices and end the war with Iran. Boebert's tenure First elected to represent Colorado's 3rd District in 2020, Boebert quickly became one of the more vocal and recognizable members of the House Republican caucus. She has been a persistent critic of the "deep state" and was a staunch supporter of Trump's efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election. During her first year in the House, she introduced separate resolutions to impeach then-President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris over their handling of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan. In 2023, she was one of the key voices behind a leadership battle among House Republicans that was only settled when Kevin McCarthy was elected Speaker after 15 roll call votes. Later that year, she mounted a second unsuccessful effort to impeach Biden. Boebert's personal life drew scrutiny in September 2023 after she and a male companion were escorted out of a stage production of Beetlejuice for allegedly "vaping, singing, [and] causing a disturbance." Though she initially denied acting inappropriately, she later apologized for her behavior, saying that her actions "fell short of my values." Though Boebert won her first House race by a comfortable margin, she narrowly avoided defeat in her bid for reelection in 2022, defeating her Democratic challenger by just 546 votes. Prior to the 2024 election, Boebert switched her reelection bid to Colorado's 4th District, a region of the state considered "far more favorable to Republicans." The move proved effective in helping Boebert secure a comfortable victory in 2024. But the redder district was not enough to insulate her from the widespread Democratic gains across the country this year. articles.title: Deadly building collapse brought Brooklyn neighbors together. Now they want answers.
articles.summary: Emergency personnel work at the scene of a partial building collapse where, according to local reports, people are trapped in the Brooklyn borough of New York, on Wednesday, November 11. - Angelina Katsanis/Reuters Leonor Yupa dropped to her knees Thursday when a Spanish-language media reporter said her 22-year-old son was among eight people whose lives were claimed by the Brooklyn building collapse the day before. “I want my son! I want my son!” the Ecuadorian mother cried in Spanish as family members tried to hold Yupa up and others who gathered at Bethesda Church of God in Christ assured her the reports were unconfirmed. The agonizing cries of another woman who just lost her husband reverberated through the Brooklyn sanctuary across the street from the collapse. When the woman learned her husband’s body was pulled from the debris Thursday morning, she collapsed and wailed her husband’s name. “Tomás! Tomasito!” she cried. Family members gathered around the widow and formed a prayer circle. Just outside the church, a nervous father also prayed. He was anxiously waiting to learn the fate of his son, a construction worker who has not been reachable since the collapse. In the Flatbush neighborhood – home to a mix of immigrant communities – six adults and two children had died and over a dozen were injured after the three-story mixed-use building collapsed on Veterans Day, a day on which many families stayed home. unknown content item - “I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told reporters Thursday. “These were our friends and our neighbors, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad, and beyond.” The day after the tragedy, residents and other bystanders crowded the sidewalk as construction equipment was used to remove debris and rubble from the site. Clothes still hung from a closet in an adjoining building where a wall came down during the collapse. A construction worker embraces a child at the scene of the collapse on Wednesday. - Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images North America/Getty Images Heavy rain pelted the intersection of Flatbush and Bedford avenues, a multicultural enclave that is the heart of New York City’s Caribbean diaspora. The names on signs of storefront churches and businesses – from bakeries, restaurants and beauty salons – reflect places like Jamaica, Haiti, Trinidad and Tobago, and more recently, newcomers from Mexico and Ecuador. Among those killed Wednesday were three Colombian citizens, two Ecuadorian men and a 26-year-old Guatemalan man, officials from the countries announced. A six months pregnant woman who was rescued from the collapse this week sustained serious injuries, but her unborn child is still alive, according to a spokesperson for her family. “By the grace of God, both she and her unborn baby are alive. However, she sustained serious injuries and is currently receiving medical care at the hospital,” Mamadou Saliou Diallo, president of the Guinean Community of America New York, said during a news conference Friday morning. The woman’s husband, Fatoumata Binta Bah, said he was returning home from getting groceries when he first saw the commotion. He went around the people gathering thinking it was a car crash, then a woman told him a building had collapsed. “When she told me that, I couldn’t feel where I was anymore. I realized that our building borders this area. I told her ‘My wife is inside, my friends are inside!’” Bah recalled. Another woman who survived the collapse said she had taken the day off from work and had been trying to go to sleep with the lights off in her room because she had a headache. Ciahola Lawrence then heard a loud thump, and when she opened her eyes there was light everywhere and an open view of the rubble. unknown content item - “I could see my neighbors coming out on stretchers – they were already dead. We didn’t deserve this!” Lawrence wailed, later pushing her head into her husband’s chest as her words dissolved into sobs. Zariah, a girl whose family survived the collapse, expressed concern over her family’s cat, who was inside the building at the time of the collapse. “They said they were inside the house to try to find him, but I don’t think they really did,” she said. “He’s hiding from them, and I think he’s scared of them, and I just really want them to come and get our cat.” unknown content item - Starting to become emotional, she said, “They put a lot of lives in danger.” After she finished speaking, Zariah was comforted by New York Attorney General Letitia James. In the aftermath of the collapse, local families, clergy and community groups gathered to support one another while demanding accountability for housing conditions and construction oversight in their predominantly Black and immigrant neighborhood. ‘Go in the church and pray, please’ On Wednesday night, Yupa and other relatives spent hours scouring hospitals throughout Brooklyn hoping to find her son, Gabriel Siguencia. The family then visited the collapse site Thursday. Yupa shielded herself from heavy rain under the canopy of the church as a woman with a West Indian lilt alerted other bystanders nearby that she saw first responders pull a young child and a woman from the rubble. Then came the news about Siguencia, who had arrived in New York from Ecuador only about a month ago and started working as a carpenter at the construction site adjacent to the building collapse about two weeks ago, according to uncles, cousins and family friends. “He came to America looking for the same opportunities that people from all over the world come here for,” said family friend Javier Ortega, who drove Siguencia’s mother to the site from her home in Connecticut. “That’s why he was working there.” Like many other families, Siguencia’s loved ones awaited news about him across the street from the collapse site. Some, like the husband of a six month pregnant woman rescued from the rubble, rejoiced as they received word their loved one was safe. unknown content item - As the downpour intensified Thursday over the neighborhood known as “Little Haiti,” a member of Bethesda Church of God in Christ invited Siguencia’s family inside the warm vestibule. Yupa, weeping, sat on a folding chair as a Haitian church member served her cups of water. As Yupa sobbed, family members surrounded her and Ecuadoran consular officials made calls trying to track down information. Soft murmurs of “Hallelujah, hallelujah” spilled out from the church filled with Haitian worshippers on the other side of the vestibule doors. “We all have to look out for each other in this country,” said the woman who brought water to Yupa and the others. “It doesn’t matter where you come from.” Another woman implored Yupa as she wept: “Go in the church and pray, please.” Time ticked by with a heaviness before officials with the Ecuadoran consul walked Yupa and her friends and family members several blocks in the heavy rain to a nearby YMCA, where relatives of the dead and missing had been gathering. The consul general of Ecuador, Gicela Andrade Valens, later told reporters outside that authorities had confirmed Siguencia’s death to his mother. Another Ecuadorian national, 26-year-old José Luis Caguana Cosquillo, was also killed. Winston Sanchez, who spoke on behalf of Cosquillo’s family, said he had left behind a pregnant wife who is due to give birth soon and that the child would never meet their father. Sanchez said he hopes the city will do more to protect construction workers. “Developers, real estate, different construction companies, they’re making a lot of money with the blood of many construction workers,” Sanchez said. “That is unacceptable, and I hope the city, on behalf of the families, will do more to protect our construction workers.” Colombia’s consulate in New York said two Colombian children and one adult were killed in the collapse. “The Consulate of Colombia in New York reiterates its most sincere condolences to the victims’ families and loved ones,” the consulate said. ‘Nothing like this has ever happened in this neighborhood’ Pastor Alfred Justin Joseph’s church, the Bethesda Church of God in Christ, became an open sanctuary for the injured, the anxious and the grieving. “They were standing in the street. I let them in,” Joseph said. “Thank God we have counselors in the church — people who do counseling for grief.” Various groups have streamed through his church, including a dozen people in the first wave. While some have since been escorted to a local YMCA or hotels, the church remains an epicenter of consolation and support. As she heard the wailing of the young woman who lost her spouse in the collapse, Flatbush resident Joy Kerr led a prayer circle to offer some comfort in a moment of devastation. Kerr walked into the church and found the young woman crying hysterically after learning that her spouse, a construction worker, was killed when the building came down. Kerr listened to the woman sobbing for about half an hour and said, “No, I can’t take this. I can’t sit back and just watch her and listen to her cry so hysterically.” “In that moment, I knew she needed comfort,” she said. She gathered with the woman who had lost her spouse and those around them, and they began to pray. “This is devastating,” Kerr said. “Nothing like this has ever happened in this neighborhood, and we just need to come together and stay together as a community.” unknown content item - And Katie Stevens, a teacher who lives about a block from the building, sobbed after she watched first responders load body bags into a van Thursday morning. “I care for my neighbors so much,” Stevens told CNN. “I’m just so sad.” James Williams, a bricklayer who has lived in the neighborhood for 35 years, stood across the street from the wreckage site Thursday and recalled watching the building’s walls cave in the day before. One image reverberated in his mind: a woman climbing a now-exposed staircase as everything around her was crumbling. “I don’t know if she got out alive or not,” he lamented. “To see that and not know what happened to her … I might have to go see a psychiatrist.” Williams said he knows multiple families affected by the collapse. A friend told him she had been texting with relatives at the site when it collapsed but had not been able to locate them at any local hospitals. As grief rippled through the neighborhood, nonprofits and agencies including the Red Cross, NYC Human Resources Administration and World Central Kitchen helped shaken families with emergency shelter, supplies and updates about missing people. Neighbors call for accountability Officials stand at the site on Thursday - Yuki Iwamura/AP As darkness fell over the collapse site Thursday night, amid thunderclaps and heavy rain, floodlights shone on a now-idle backhoe that had been excavating piles of debris, twisted metal and the pieces of what had been apartments into dumpsters. Crews finished a marathon search through the rubble and determined there were no more survivors to be rescued, officials had said Thursday afternoon. Under umbrellas, people hurried home after work, some stopping momentarily to look at the now-vacant space that had recently been home to many. Across the street, a cluster of older women started gathering early for an evening service at Bethesda Church of God in Christ. “This church happens to be a Haitian Creole speaking church, but the church is open to the entire community,” said Florence Saint-Jean, a psychologist who offers mental health and trauma services at the church. “The people who live here are immigrants, and so when crisis happens, there’s only one language – love,” she said. “People are tired, they’re looking for food, they’re looking for shelter, and the church is always open and available.” The New York City Public Advocate – who serves as an ombudsman for citizen complaints – said Friday many local residents are afraid to speak up when they see violations. “We have the intersection of immigration and people afraid to come out and speak,” Jumanne Williams said. “We want to make sure we’re speaking up for them.” As neighbors hugged and comforted one another, one question created knots in their chests: How could this tragedy have happened? The Department of Buildings has not yet determined the cause of the collapse, and an investigation is underway as new information emerges about the building’s history and construction process. Residents of three buildings on the block are still barred from their homes, and questions are growing over whether the developers were digging for a much larger building than the city approved. Department of Buildings sweeps “have now expanded their scope to more than 160 sites across our city, associated with six entities that are associated with this project,” Mamdani said Friday, adding an outside engineering consulting firm will also provide an independent report. “If we find anyone that has violated the law, we will hold them fully accountable,” the mayor said. The Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office is conducting its own investigation into whether laws were broken at the site of the collapse. “We’re looking at the entire history, and if there are additional things that we need to see, that will be part of the investigation,” Department of Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said Friday. As investigators try to determine factors in Wednesday’s deadly collapse of the three-story building in Brooklyn, they’ll be looking at both the condition of the collapsed building and activity at the construction site that neighbored it. Cracks had been reported in the facade of the building as part of the permitting process for construction on the adjacent lot, which the collapse spilled into. The building’s owner, Olufemi Falade , has a troubling history that reportedly landed him in jail for 12 days in 2006 for failing to repair hundreds of violations across multiple buildings. Falade was frequently listed on the annual Worst Landlords Watchlist put out by the New York City Public Advocate’s office, although he is not on the most recent list. “I don’t want to speak out of turn. I want to wait for the investigation to outplay,” Williams said. “But I will say if you have multiple negligence, both on the owner’s side and/or the construction side, there definitely should be a criminal investigation and, I believe, arrests at some point if that is the case.” CNN has reached out to Falade for comment. The collapsed building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue currently has 98 open housing violations – ranging from unsafe electrical wiring and a lack of smoke detectors to bedbug infestations and a lack of adequate water supply for the building’s sprinkler system – according to records from the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development. Local election officials promised to address understaffing in the city’s Department of Buildings. “Right now, the building department has an 8 to 9% vacancy rate,” said New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin. “We will ensure that every single one of those positions is immediately filled.” Though building collapses are rare in the US, lower-income and immigrant neighborhoods often face higher risks of hazards and neglect. Housing experts and advocates have pointed to systemic inequities that disproportionately impact working class immigrant communities, including old buildings, lax code enforcement and rapid construction. Sumathy Kumar, executive director of New York State Tenant Bloc and Housing Justice for All, an organization that works to organize tenants, said the Brooklyn landlord has an extensive and troubling history with the city. “We need better and faster tools to hold landlords accountable and to make sure that buildings are properly maintained and managed,” Kumar said. Saint-Jean said there is a visible distinction between how development occurs in immigrant communities like Flatbush. “What we’re most concerned about is, when things like his happen, that our voice (is) not being heard about development in the area,” she said. articles.title: Murdaugh seeks to toss murder indictments over what investigator told grand jury
articles.summary: Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh asked a judge Friday to throw out the original murder indictments for killing his wife and son, saying the chief investigator in the case lied to the grand jury. Murdaugh is facing a retrial on the murder charges after the South Carolina Supreme Court threw out his convictions and life sentence, ruling that a court clerk improperly influenced jurors against him during his 2023 trial . Even if the request to dismiss the indictments is granted, it may not stop or even postpone an April retrial for the disgraced lawyer. Prosecutors can seek another set of grand jury indictments, and defense attorneys said they won't stop them. Judge ends hearing with interesting question Judge Debra McCaslin did not immediately decide on the defense request, promising a written ruling next week. But one of her last comments at the hearing may have indicated where she is going. "If you had to go back to the grand jury, could you have it all done and ready to go by April 5th?" she asked prosecutor Creighton Waters. "Your honor, I'm always working ahead," Waters responded. Throwing out indictments could be another rebuke of agent on case A ruling throwing out the indictments would be another rebuke of the chief investigator in Murdaugh's case, State Law Enforcement Division agent David Owen. A judge last year threw out a different murder case Owen was involved in because the dead woman's mother told the agent about a suicide threat her daughter made days before she died that Owen never relayed to prosecutors or defense attorneys. She was found dead by the same method she told her mother she was going to use to kill herself. Owen abruptly retired in 2024, not long after he was honored as State Law Enforcement Officer of the Year. Prosecutors pointed out while Owen is accused of hiding or not revealing evidence in that case, all the issues in the Murdaugh case involved evidence and reports the defense had at the original trial. The grand jury heard several questionable assertions Prosecutors said Murdaugh, 58, killed his wife, Maggie, and younger son, Paul, on their sprawling property in the South Carolina Lowcountry in 2021. Murdaugh is spending decades in prison for stealing millions of dollars from clients, and has admitted in court that he is a thief, insurance cheat, bad lawyer and longtime opioid addict. But he denies being a killer. Defense lawyers said that as prosecutors sought the indictments, Owen told the Colleton County grand jury that blood spatter was found on a T-shirt Murdaugh was wearing the night of the killings. An earlier report from state agents said there were no blood stains, and no such evidence was introduced at trial. Owen also told grand jurors that the same ammunition load of buckshot in one chamber and large birdshot in the other used to kill Paul Murdaugh was found loaded in weapons all over the Murdaugh property, which wasn't the case. The grand jury may have heard about plenty of evidence, including the video Paul Murdaugh recorded in which Alex Murdaugh's voice could be heard at the scene, contradicting his claims that he wasn't at the kennels near where his wife and son were killed any time close to their deaths. But defense attorney Jim Griffin said the false evidence of the blood of Murdaugh's son was the only thing anyone heard that could link him to the place and time of the killings. "A phone call doesn't put him there. The video doesn't put him there," Griffin said. "The blood from his murdered son sprang through the air — it's raining back on him — puts him there." Prosecutors call it a mistake, cite other evidence against Murdaugh Prosecutors said they had plenty of other evidence supporting the murder charges, and wrote in court papers that "a single mistake is not bad faith." Along with the kennel video, Owen told the grand jury about the family's mounting debts, guns missing from the house that matched what could have been used in the killings and how Murdaugh's schemes to steal from clients and his law firm were close to being discovered. "This is what the agent understood at the time. And it's ultimately not something that would cause a substantial effect on the grand jury or cast grave doubt when we look at all the other evidence that was presented," Waters said. Prosecutors said Murdaugh killed his wife and son because he thought the sympathy generated by the killings would buy him time to cover up his thefts. Murdaugh's lawyers have repeatedly pointed out how little evidence prosecutors have. No DNA or blood was found splattered on Murdaugh or any of his clothes, even though the killings were at close range with powerful weapons that were never found. "What we're asking, your honor, is to reboot — go back to square one," Griffin said. Even with the original convictions overturned, Murdaugh remains in prison on separate financial crime sentences . The outcome of the murder case will not determine when he could be released. articles.title: Winter weather hits the East, but a big temperature swing is just days away
articles.summary: Heading into the weekend, a Northeast storm will continue to bring rain and snow to the region before a blast of winter cold moves in, according to AccuWeather meteorologists. While the steadier snow from a nor'easter across the interior Northeast will end on Friday, lake-effect rain and snow showers will develop on Saturday as colder air settles in across the region. Parts of New York and Vermont could see the greatest snow accumulations, with forecasts of 6 to 12 inches of wet snow, which can weigh down tree branches and cause power outages. Major northeastern cities including New York City, Philadelphia and Boston are expected to face travel disruptions due to rain and blustery conditions. "Rain, low clouds and aircraft deicing could contribute to flight delays," according to AccuWeather. Some areas could also experience their coldest temperatures since March. Freezing temperatures are forecast to reach the Deep South by Saturday morning, setting up a widespread frost and freeze across the South and Southeast this weekend. As of Friday afternoon, over 39 million Americans were under a freeze warning issued by the National Weather Service. But there will be a reprieve from the winter-like weather just around the corner. "People dealing with snow and bitterly cold winds this weekend could be enjoying much milder weather just days later," according to AccuWeather meteorologist Haley Taylor. "November can bring some dramatic temperature swings, and this is a good example of how quickly the atmosphere can change gears. The same areas getting a taste of winter now could see a stretch of dry weather and temperatures well above average next week." Thursday's nor'easter produced snow, hail and tornadoes Parts of the northeast, including Syracuse, Binghamton and Pittsburgh, saw their first snowflakes of the season. Leonardsville, in central New York, received the most snow overnight, with 13.2 inches as of 10 a.m. ET on Friday, according to the National Weather Service . More snow could be on the way into the weekend. "Several inches or more of wet, clinging snow could accumulate across parts of West Virginia, northeast Pennsylvania, the Catskills, the Adirondacks and the Green and White Mountains, with significant accumulations possible on the ridges," said AccuWeather . Meanwhile, severe storms brought reports of tornadoes to parts of Delaware and New Jersey, and hail in the Philadelphia suburbs. That's hail, not snow! 🧊 Severe thunderstorms swept through southeastern Pennsylvania on Thursday, leaving piles of hail up to 19 inches deep and forcing a road closure in Brookhaven. pic.twitter.com/MHxHiO0Typ — AccuWeather (@accuweather) November 13, 2026 Is the nor'easter linked to the polar vortex? The early weakening of the polar vortex , which started last week, has left many wondering whether a blast of icy weather is on its way as a result. But forecasters have said it's not that clear. While the WPC's latest forecast refers to polar air, meaning a mass of very cold air from Canada, it doesn't mention the polar vortex. Tyler Roys, a meteorologist at AccuWeather, told Yahoo it is "hard to say if there is any connection between the two." He said most of the impacts from an early polar vortex disruption are "going towards eastern Europe and Asia." If the vortex has any influence, Roys said, it is likely tied to the cold arriving behind the storm, though "the influence of the polar vortex appears to be limited." Roys added that forecasters "do feel that there could be an increase of influence from the polar vortex towards the end of November into December" as the current pattern fades and a new one sets up. Laura Ciasto, a meteorologist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), told Yahoo that the vortex has been "displaced for well over a week," though it hasn't yet reached the threshold for a sudden stratospheric warming, a rapid warming high in the atmosphere that can weaken or split the vortex. "It's possible we are seeing that effect at the surface now," she said. "It's a classic chicken-or-the-egg situation." What is a nor'easter? Areas such as North Wildwood, N.J., were hit by an unusually strong nor'easter in September. Ryan Murphy via Getty Images A nor'easter is a storm situated along the East Coast of the U.S., with its namesake reflecting that the winds over the coastal area are usually from the northeast, the NWS says. It forms when an area of lower air pressure draws in surrounding air and strengthens near the coast. It is often fueled by the clash of cold air from the north and warm, moist air over the Gulf Stream. While these storms can happen at any time of year, they are usually at their strongest between the colder months, from September through April. Nor'easters "nearly always" bring precipitation in the form of heavy rain or snow, the NWS says, as well as winds of gale force, rough seas and, sometimes, coastal flooding. The most violent nor'easters have caused billions of dollars in damage. The storm is expected to be less severe than September's early-season nor'easter, which killed a New York City Housing Authority worker , flooded coastal communities and left more than 130,000 customers without power across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, the Associated Press reported. articles.title: Trump's midterm setback leaves some longtime supporters questioning MAGA's future
articles.summary: COLUMBUS, Ohio - The young Republicans had grown restless even before their disastrous election, tired of President Donald Trump, his war and his handpicked candidates. Now about a dozen members of Ohio State University College Republicans plopped down their backpacks for their first meeting since the election and pondered what was next. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. Abraham Dixon, 20, used to identify with Trump's "Make America Great Again" movement. But MAGA seemed synonymous with loyalty to Trump, and he'd come to think of Trump as "the anchor around the elephant's neck." He worried that even a politically diminished Trump would keep bending the party to his will - and compared him to the aging emperor villain of Star Wars. "He's Palpatine," Dixon said. It was hard to picture the GOP without the man who defined it for a decade. Trump's GOP was all they knew: Many cast their first votes for him. But chapter president Hunter Willmitch was blunt in an interview about the changes underway: "The MAGA movement, in my opinion, is dead." MAGA is certainly muddled, as its rank-and-file voters look to leaders outside of the Trump administration, have crossed over to Democrats or disengaged from politics altogether. There is no consensus about who should run in 2028 and plenty of skepticism for Vice President JD Vance, who once seemed the heir apparent. Like Trump or not, everyone agrees his vacuum will be hard to fill. Right-wing influencers increasingly critical of Trump were declaring themselves vindicated by his rebuke in the midterms. Extremists like Nick Fuentes, the white-supremacist influencer, saw the chaos on the right as an opportunity. "We could not have asked for a better outcome," Fuentes declared on his live stream. It was a moment of both peril and opportunity for the Ohio State College Republicans who held their meeting in an empty classroom one night this week. "How are you?" a young woman asked Willmitch as she sat down. "Upset at the amount of losses we took," Willmitch said. "Tuesday was rough," she said. "I thought it was going to be a little rough," Willmitch echoed. "I just didn't expect … that." He mentioned the bright spot in Florida, where Republicans had weathered the blue wave and Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) was preparing another presidential bid. "If it's not for Ron DeSantis, that [state] probably flips," Willmitch said. He liked what he was hearing from the Florida governor, a longtime champion of the culture wars who now said Republicans needed to stop "fighting yesterday's battle" - prioritizing issues like the rise of artificial intelligence rather than pouring money into ads about transgender issues. Dixon agreed that the party's best bet was someone outside the Trump administration like DeSantis. He snorted when another student brought up Trump's latest interview on "60 Minutes," in which he suggested he wanted to compromise with Democrats on immigration. Republicans were like "a dog under the dinner table," the other student vented, told to be grateful for what Trump handed them. He wanted the party to run more staunch conservatives and talk more about the new populist issues animating both the right and the left: Flock cameras and data centers. Ohio state Rep. Brian Stewart (R), an Ohio State alumnus, was there as a guest speaker and was frank about the party's struggles this election cycle. Yes, Republicans were drawn into fighting old battles, he said, but "part of it too is we didn't have a lot of good things to say." A student asked him what the GOP should look like after Trump, and Stewart said Trump's overhaul of the party would endure in "the way we interact with the media, the way we sort of address questions, the way we sort of take criticism." "There used to be this just this defensive crouch that every Republican officeholder had," Stewart said - no longer. Yet Republicans couldn't just mimic Trump, he warned. The president had long defied political gravity, saying and doing things that other politicians would never get away with. He said other elected officials would need to abide by "a baseline of kindness and respectability." "We need voters to like us." A 'Front Row Joe' packs up Rick Frazier's living room was still plastered with mementos from his decade as one of Trump's "Front Row Joes" who followed him to rallies around the country. There was his picture with Trump, signed in gold pen. There was his photo with another Trump superfan best known as "Brick Suit." There was the framed letter he got from Trump in 2023 after his daughter died of a drug overdose. "Melania and I are devastated," the letter read. Frazier, 70, had thrown himself into the MAGA movement more fervently than almost anyone in the country, hooked from the moment Trump came down a golden escalator in 2015. Retired from a factory that made tank tracks for the military, he believed Trump would "drain the swamp" and help American industry. Now Frazier was done with him. From his couch in western Ohio, he laughed along at an episode of the comedy show "South Park," which has brutally and crudely skewered Trump and his administration over the past year. "He's the king of swamp," he said. Frazier's shift unfolded gradually, he said. He barely spoke about it with the other Front Row Joes - most of whom still adored Trump. He didn't like it when Trump resisted his supporters' push to release the government's full files on the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and he cringed when Trump, from the rally stage, mocked the word "affordability." He voted for Trump to straighten out the southern border and crack down on the drug trade that stole his daughter, and he couldn't make sense of Trump's decision last year to pardon a former Honduran president convicted for overseeing a "narco-state" that routed cocaine to the United States. "See, that got me all upset," he said, his voice wavering. His last Trump rally was in Kentucky, where the president railed against Rep. Thomas Massie (R), a rebellious Republican whom Frazier liked. When the midterms came, Frazier voted for his longtime Republican congressman Jim Jordan but also backed Democrats for governor and Senate, helping to flip Ohio blue. This week, he watched live as Massie unsuccessfully moved to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war with Iran. "I'm kind of going to go back to the way I was before Trump," Frazier said. "I was independently swinging wherever the best guy was running. And that's the way I think it should be. " Frazier still liked Vance, whom he's met, and thought the vice president was being honest about Republicans' missteps. "The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote on X the day after the midterm elections. But Frazier and plenty of other Trump voters were up for grabs now - and it wasn't clear who could turn him into a Front Row Joe again. 'Nobody worth voting for' At a chicken wing chain in southern Ohio, Heather Romine said she was raised to believe that you can't complain about things if you don't do something about it. So she cast a ballot in every election after she turned 18 - until last week. The 38-year-old conservative voted for Trump, but at some point in his second term, she just stopped following what was happening. "I can't keep up with it," Romine said at the bar, seated next to her boyfriend, who still liked Trump. "I don't want to keep up with it. It's defeating. It feels like it doesn't matter." "There's not a better candidate," her boyfriend said. "Nobody worth voting for," Romine replied. Her rural, working class community in Pike County, Ohio had swung harder to the right in the Trump era than almost anywhere in the country, embodying MAGA's rise. Voters heard Trump's outsider pitch and thought he would be different from other politicians. Now Romine struggled to say what could motivate her to vote again. Republicans won Pike County by a little more than 30 points last week compared to more than 50 points in 2024, in part because people stayed home. "I feel like I'm just a silent person on the sidelines right now, watching the ship burn," Romine said. She voted for Trump because she thought he would "get s--t done," but she felt she got chaos with tariffs and a war that upended the global economy. She owned a house and had a good job in health care, but with three kids, she still felt strained. She could spend $400 on a trip to the grocery store and lost track of how many times she helped buy food over the past year for a friend, a struggling single mother of two. She wanted the country to get back to something more like the "America First" vision Trump pitched - a sentiment others shared. "I think his America First agenda was a good idea, but I don't think he stuck to that," said Brandon Williams, a 46-year-old firefighter who voted three times for Trump. "So I would like to see somebody run somewhere on that same line, but actually do that." Plenty of people in town still supported Trump and thought he was doing the best he could. The war wasn't great, they said, but he closed the borders and pushed back on ideas about gender identity that disturbed them. They were all over the map, however, about who could follow Trump in 2028 and if MAGA would hold together. They were more familiar than most with Vance, an Ohio native who briefly represented the state in the Senate. But they often weren't sure about him and struggled to put their finger on why. "I just don't know, said Rick Patrick, 74, who prefers Secretary of State Marco Rubio. "It's a feeling." Diane Alley, a retired nurse, worried no one could recapture what Trump had stirred up here. "I'm terrified," she said as she made her way through the grocery store. "I don't know who they can run. Nobody is going to equal him." A White House spokesperson pointed to Trump's comments on "60 Minutes" that he thinks MAGA can continue without him. "Because MAGA is basically common sense … strong borders, good military," Trump said. But the president said Republicans would have done better last week if he were on the ballot, "because you saw the level of popularity and love." "There was love," he said. articles.title: U.S. reportedly offered little help as Singapore probed Nvidia chip shipments
articles.summary: Singaporean authorities seized the passport of then-Megaspeed chief executive Alice Huang in June 2025 and held it for eight months, preventing her departure while trying to engage the U.S. government to support their investigation into advanced Nvidia chips possibly being shipped to China . One source with knowledge of the matter told CBS News on Friday the Singaporean government received no meaningful help from Washington during the time she was in the Asian city-state. This source said officials in Washington were "not forthcoming" in response to Singapore's requests for help, and no substantive assistance has been provided to date. Singapore's government confirmed in a statement this week that it reached out to both the U.S. Department of Justice and the FBI for assistance with its investigation. Alice Huang is the suspected Chinese spy at the center of the extramarital affair scandal that toppled Nvidia founder Jensen Huang from the helm of the global tech giant he built over three decades. Since February 2025, Singaporean authorities have been investigating whether Alice Huang and Megaspeed worked with California-based Supermicro to ship the Silicon Valley firm's computer servers — equipped with advanced Nvidia chips — to China, the source told CBS News. Alice Huang flew into Singapore in June 2025 for a voluntary interview with Singapore-based investigators from the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security, according to the source. The agency sits within the U.S. Department of Commerce and regulates the export of sensitive products on national security and economic grounds. The American authorities requested the interview, according to a Thursday statement by Singapore's Home Affairs Ministry, as part of a post-shipment verification check, a process used to determine whether imported products have reached their declared recipient. Singaporean police also interviewed Huang on the same day as the U.S. officials, and made the decision to impound her passport. The source said it was not known where Huang, a Chinese national, arrived in Singapore from in June 2025. By February 2026, however, the Singapore Police Force had not charged Huang with any crime and had no option but to return her passport, the source told CBS News. She was barred from ever returning to Singapore, as authorities assessed that she had given "inaccurate information" to downplay her role at Megaspeed, as noted in the statement from the home ministry. That statement was released four days after Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who sources confirmed to CBS News was Alice Huang. Singapore's investigation has focused on whether the then-Megaspeed CEO may have broken domestic law by lying about the details of purchases of computer servers from Supermicro, a San Jose-based technology company. The company's servers use Nvidia's advanced chips to run artificial intelligence software, data centers and cloud computing. "The suspected domestic offenses pertained to potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offenses," Singapore's Home Affairs Ministry said in its statement this week. Singaporean investigators have tried to determine the true ultimate destination of the Supermicro servers ordered by Megaspeed. A second source familiar with the investigation told CBS News it is believed they may have been sent to Malaysia, but Singaporean investigators suspect "some or all" of them may then have been shipped onward to China. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing. Singapore's home ministry attempted to contact Supermicro, but the U.S. company only "provided limited cooperation," according to the home ministry statement. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Malaysia kept Nvidia's chips and installed them in its own data centers, but then rented use of those centers to China, rather than physically shipping any chips to China. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Friday that there was "no indication" any chips linked to the Nvidia-Megaspeed issue had been re-exported out of the country. Beijing has dismissed the claims that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy as "groundless speculation" and "nothing more than an attempt to smear China." Asked Thursday about a Bloomberg report that she had returned to China, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters: "I do not have information on what you mentioned." Since 2022, the U.S. has restricted the export of Nvidia's most powerful chips to China over national security concerns as the world's two biggest economies race for dominance in the AI sector . The Singapore police first raised the issue with U.S. authorities in July 2025 to try to secure Supermicro's cooperation in revealing where its servers were ultimately ending up, repeating requests "on several occasions to the U.S. Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation," according to the Home Affairs Ministry's Thursday statement. The second source confirmed to CBS News that Washington did not meaningfully engage with the requests for help on the investigation and said it "would be useful to know" what Supermicro declared about its exports to fulfill orders by Megaspeed, whether those products were registered as being bound for Malaysia, and whether some or all of those products were actually "bound for somewhere else," such as China. The Singapore home ministry said in its statement that six other individuals linked to Megaspeed, in addition to Alice Huang, are wanted for questioning, but none have been in the country since the government launched its investigation in February 2025. "One is a Singaporean citizen and the rest are foreigners," said the first person familiar with the case. Singapore has charged five other people in a wider fraud conspiracy case related to the suspected transfer of Nvidia chips, including one Chinese man charged on Friday. The case was launched at the same time as the probe into Alice Huang and Megaspeed, the first source told CBS News, but it is separate. "Singapore is committed to upholding our reputation as a trusted and reliable business hub. We will not allow companies or individuals to misuse Singapore's business environment to engage in fraud or dishonest practices," the home ministry said in its statement, adding that it would "conduct its own investigations independently, in accordance with our laws and based on the evidence available. We will cooperate with foreign authorities where appropriate, and take firm enforcement action wherever the evidence warrants it." articles.title: Bessent points finger at Lutnick over Nvidia chip exports
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before lawmakers next month as the spotlight on him grows harsher amid Nvidia's ( NVDA ) turmoil. Both Democrats and Republicans alike are raising questions about whether Lutnick went too far in protecting Nvidia's push to sell its chips overseas even as the US government was warning about a possible security breach. Lutnick is reportedly set to appear on Dec. 10 before the Senate Banking Committee, in news first reported by Fox News. Spokespersons for the Commerce Department and the Senate panel did not immediately provide additional details. The appearance would set up what could be a major moment for the suddenly embattled Commerce secretary after days in which he and the White House had largely stayed silent as even some of Trump's closest allies grew more vocal. Lutnick will appear before Republican Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the Senate panel until the end of the year and a regular on President Trump's campaign stops last month. Scott released a letter Thursday evening requesting that Lutnick and ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appear before Congress early next month. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Scott wrote. "The American people deserve answers." Then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick listen in the Oval Office during an unrelated event in July. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images) Chip Somodevilla via Getty Images Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana used more colorful language in a recent appearance on CNN , saying he wanted answers about why the Commerce Department allowed Nvidia to sell chips to an alleged Chinese spy's company. "This whole thing is an intergalactic freak show," Kennedy said. Some Trump aides have declined to defend Lutnick emphatically. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent raised eyebrows Friday during a CNBC appearance when he reiterated his desire for stronger government limits on advanced semiconductor exports — which he added that the Pentagon, State Department, and the trade representative's office agreed with. "Commerce has the pen…," Bessent said, "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes." The rapid-fire developments have also increased the odds of Congress passing new curbs on semiconductor exports to China, with lawmakers now moving to add some combination of three bipartisan plans into a military funding bill that needs to pass before the end of the year. A White House official said that Trump maintains confidence in Lutnick, but the president's only direct reaction to the scandal in recent days was a Truth Social post saying Huang had "done a fantastic job" and that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over Nvidia. The administration's response has done little to quell the questions from lawmakers after reports about whether Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy endangered US national security and painted Lutnick as a roadblock in responding, even as other Trump aides pushed for more muscular action. The New York Times reported that Trump was warned about the possible security issues with Nvidia on two separate occasions but didn't act. Secretary Lutnick speaks during a midterm campaign rally with President Donald Trump in North Carolina in October. (Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images) KENT NISHIMURA via Getty Images These questions have led to a flurry of calls for investigations and for Lutnick and Huang to testify. Huang has agreed to appear before a House panel before Thanksgiving, though a date hasn't been set yet. Republican Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana said he wants to hear from Lutnick soon "because we have a lot of bipartisan questions and concerns about what's happened over the last year." Democrats are set to take control of the House and Senate committees that oversee trade and have already launched an investigation into Lutnick. The flood of criticism has led senior White House officials to discuss whether Lutnick should be pushed out, according to a Reuters report , but it is not yet clear if Trump is willing to jettison a close ally who has survived other accusations in the first two years of Trump's second term. This spring, Lutnick was forced to revise his account of his ties to Jeffrey Epstein after the release of the disgraced financier's files revealed that Lutnick had contact with Epstein for years longer than he had previously claimed. Lutnick was forced to testify before Congress about the matter — and Democrats called it an embarrassing episode — but Trump stood by him. articles.title: 索罗斯基金Q3大举加码英特尔、Meta，新进SK海力士，减持英伟达
articles.summary: 索罗斯基金管理公司（Soros Fund Management）2026年第三季度大幅调整美股持仓：新建仓韩国存储芯片巨头SK海力士ADR，大幅增持英特尔和Meta，同时减持英伟达，并清仓KKR和ServiceNow。 从持仓变化看，该基金在继续布局AI产业链的同时，对芯片行业内部的配置进行了调整。英特尔和Meta获得大幅加仓，英伟达普通股持仓则有所下降，SK海力士的加入也使其投资组合进一步覆盖AI存储领域。 根据SEC第三季度13F文件，截至2026年9月30日，索罗斯基金披露的持仓涉及247项投资，据统计，13F组合市值约为64.81亿美元。 新进SK海力士ADR，布局AI存储产业链 第三季度，索罗斯基金新建仓韩国存储芯片制造商SK海力士（SK Hynix）的美国存托凭证（ADR），持有32.5万股，披露持仓市值约5985万美元。 SK海力士是全球主要存储芯片制造商之一，也是AI数据中心高带宽内存（HBM）供应链的重要参与者。随着AI服务器和加速计算需求增长，HBM已成为AI芯片产业链的重要环节。 此次新建仓SK海力士，意味着索罗斯基金的美股组合新增了AI存储领域的重要标的。 英特尔持仓激增28倍，Meta增持近六倍 美国科技股方面，索罗斯基金第三季度大幅增持英特尔（INTC）和Meta（META）。 其中，英特尔持仓从第二季度末的10万股增至283万股，增加273万股，增幅高达2730%，相当于持仓规模扩大至原来的28.3倍。截至三季度末，英特尔持仓市值约3.40亿美元。 Meta方面，持股数量从第二季度末的21776股增至15.15万股，增加约12.97万股，增幅约596%，三季度末持仓市值约1.10亿美元。 两只股票均获得大幅加仓，显示索罗斯基金在第三季度明显增加了对美国大型科技公司的配置。 减持英伟达，普通股与看跌期权分别披露 与英特尔获得大幅增持形成对比，索罗斯基金第三季度减持了英伟达（NVDA）普通股。 截至三季度末，该基金持有英伟达普通股约85.88万股，较第二季度末的106.46万股减少约20.58万股，降幅约19.3%。三季度末普通股持仓市值约1.96亿美元。 此外，13F文件还单独披露了英伟达看跌期权仓位，对应的持仓数量从第二季度末的40万股降至35万股，期权披露市值约7993万美元。 需要注意的是，普通股与看跌期权属于不同类型的持仓，不能合并计算为英伟达股票持股数量。期权披露数量也不等同于期权合约份数。 清仓KKR、ServiceNow，退出部分金融和软件股 在其他个股方面，索罗斯基金第三季度退出了部分此前持有的股票。 其中，KKR（KKR）第二季度末持有88715股，第三季度末已不再出现在13F持仓表中；ServiceNow（NOW）第二季度末持有48570股，第三季度同样退出披露组合。 两项持仓第二季度末的披露市值分别约814万美元和482万美元。 整体来看，索罗斯基金第三季度的调仓呈现出较为鲜明的科技股配置变化：新进SK海力士ADR，大幅增持英特尔和Meta，同时降低英伟达普通股敞口，并退出KKR和ServiceNow。 不过，13F文件仅反映基金截至季度末的部分美国市场证券多头持仓，不披露完整的全球资产配置、空头头寸及现金，也无法揭示具体交易时间和投资决策原因。因此，这些变化反映的是其季度末披露组合的调整，并不意味着基金对相关公司的投资观点必然发生了相应变化。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 避免流动性支持被视为QE，美联储洛根提议市场功能性购债单独记账、尽快出售
articles.summary: 美联储官员正推动对央行资产负债表管理框架进行结构性调整，核心诉求是 将市场功能性购债与货币政策操作彻底分离，以消除市场对流动性干预是否变相压制长端收益率的疑虑。 达拉斯联储主席Lorie Logan（洛根）周四在达拉斯联储联合主办的银行融资会议上表示， 美联储应将为维护市场功能而购入的资产单独记账，并承诺尽快出售，以防此类操作在无意间提供额外刺激。 她同时指出，国债收益率的快速攀升本身并不必然意味着市场出现了需要央行介入的失序状态，联储更依赖买卖价差、市场深度和价格冲击等流动性指标作为研判依据。 上述表态折射出美联储内部对危机时期市场干预与量化宽松界限模糊问题的持续关注。 官员们历来依靠沟通来划清两者边界，但投资者始终存有疑问：若政策制定者希望避免外界将流动性操作与压制长端收益率挂钩，是否需要为平仓路径建立更明确的机制。 资产分账管理：化解市场疑虑的核心主张 Logan明确提出了多种方案，以更清晰地区分市场功能性操作与货币政策执行。 最具操作性的建议是：联邦公开市场委员会将因市场功能目的购入的证券存入独立账户，并公开承诺尽快出售，从而在机制层面为两类操作划定硬边界。 她强调， 市场对联储决策逻辑的充分理解本身就具有稳定功能。 "公众对联邦公开市场委员会策略有更清晰的认知，能够增强市场对自身持续正常运转的信心。而当市场参与者有信心时，他们就会持续交易，这反而降低了联储可能需要介入的概率。"Logan表示。 资产负债表工作组：改革路线图渐趋明朗 这一讨论发生在美联储启动系统性审视资产负债表管理框架的背景之下。 美联储主席沃什于今年5月就任后，召集五个外部专家工作组研究关键议题，其中包括资产负债表问题。 沃什上月表示，负责该议题的工作组建议预计将于2027年第一季度出炉，届后政策制定者将就相关提案展开审议。 资产负债表工作组由前美联储理事Jeremy Stein、印度储备银行前行长Raghuram Rajan以及哈佛大学经济学教授Karen Dynan共同领导， 核心任务是探索如何缩减美联储在市场中的直接介入规模——这也是沃什长期以来的施政优先项之一。 应急融资机制：扩容与常态化并举 Logan在讲话中还就金融机构的流动性压力应对提出具体建议。她呼吁银行及其他金融机构尽可能做好充分准备，包括提前具备使用联储应急贷款工具的条件，而非等到危机爆发才临时寻求支持。 Logan还表示， 被认定为对金融系统运转至关重要的"指定金融市场基础设施"（DFMU）在极端情形下也应获准使用贴现窗口借款，且该应急融资工具应在周末和节假日照常运作。 这一主张指向当前机制在时间覆盖上存在的潜在缺口，旨在确保流动性支持在关键时刻不因时间因素出现中断。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 高盛2027年宏观展望：全球经济略为提速但道路崎岖，下行风险不容忽视
articles.summary: 全球经济在经历2026年伊朗战争冲击后展现出超预期韧性，但高盛警告，2027年的增长路径将更为崎岖，风险天平明显向下倾斜。 高盛首席经济学家Jan Hatzius领衔撰写的2027年宏观展望报告预测，全球GDP增速将从2026年的2.7%小幅升至2.8%，略高于潜在增速。 报告的核心判断是：能源价格正常化与持续强劲的AI资本开支将构成主要支撑，但金融条件收紧与财政刺激退潮将形成对冲，整体增长格局"稳健但平淡"。与此同时，高盛明确指出三大下行风险——伊朗局势再度升级、债券市场动荡以及AI投资周期提前见顶——并认为市场面临的挑战将比宏观经济本身更为严峻。 在货币政策层面，高盛预计美联储将在12月和明年3月各加息一次，欧洲央行将在12月完成最后一次加息，随后两家央行均将于2027年底转向降息。高盛的利率预测整体较市场定价更为鸽派，这一判断对股票和债券均构成潜在利好。在资产配置上，高盛维持股票和债券正回报的基线预测，但强调随着市场周期趋于成熟，波动性上升的概率大于下降，建议投资者加强对冲与分散配置。 增长动能切换：能源转顺风，AI投资仍是主引擎 2026年，AI资本开支激增、金融条件宽松以及美国、德国等经济体的财政扩张，基本抵消了伊朗战争引发的能源供给冲击，全球经济实现2.7%的增长，仅较高盛此前预测低0.1个百分点。中国台湾和韩国因AI出口激增而显著跑赢，分别超预期8.6个百分点和1.9个百分点，美国和欧元区则小幅落后。 展望2027年，能源价格冲击预计将从阻力转为助力。高盛大宗商品策略师的基线预测显示，布伦特原油价格将于2027年底降至78美元/桶，全球LNG价格同步正常化，能源价格对全球增长的拖累将从2026年的0.4个百分点转为小幅提振。 AI资本开支仍是最重要的增长引擎。高盛预测，全球名义AI投资规模将从2026年的1.1万亿美元增至2027年的1.8万亿美元，增量主要来自美国硬件支出超过5000亿美元的提升。AI投资将为全球GDP增速贡献约0.4个百分点，其中对剔除半导体投资及芯片相关知识产权出口的统计低估后的美国“真实”GDP增速的贡献估计达0.6个百分点。 财政与金融条件方面，高盛GS金融条件指数（GS FCI）过去三个月在美国收紧约50个基点、在发达市场收紧约30个基点，将对未来几个季度的增长形成温和拖累。财政扩张的边际效应也在消退，主要例外是日本——消费税削减、国防支出增加及高市政府投资计划预计将为日本GDP增速带来0.7个百分点的提振。 在主要经济体预测中，高盛对美国经济增长持相对乐观态度，预计增速2.4%，高于市场一致预期2.2%，对欧洲则更为悲观，预计增速0.9%，低于一致预期1.3%，主要原因是金融条件收紧以及能源价格高企将在今冬开始显现。高盛预测中国增速为4.5%，略高于市场一致预期4.4%。 三大下行风险：能源、债市与AI周期 高盛明确将2027年全球增长风险定性为偏向下行，并列举三条主要路径。 伊朗局势再度升级。 高盛大宗商品策略师在基线预测之外，赋予更大权重的上行情景是：航运攻击加剧、石油基础设施受损以及更持久的风险溢价，可能将油价推升至132美元/桶。若该情景成真，能源价格冲击将在2027年继续拖累全球增长，且与2026年不同，届时金融条件和财政政策已难以提供同等程度的对冲。 债市动荡。 发达市场收益率曲线目前较2026年初高出约85个基点。高盛估计，若这一升幅持续，将通过住房、耐用消费品和企业投资渠道累计拖累GDP约0.5%。法国的财政风险尤为突出——10年期法国国债（OAT）收益率较德国国债高出约150个基点，财政健康指标已亮起红灯。高盛预计，在法国2027年4月总统大选和6月议会选举结束前，实质性财政整顿讨论不会启动，但市场可能提前施压，形成更大的增长拖累。 AI投资冲击减弱。 高盛指出，超大规模云服务商（hyperscaler）股价对财报电话会议中更高资本开支信号的反应，已从2024至2025年的正面转为2026年的略微负面，市场开始担忧过度投资。此外，第三季度财报季中超大规模企业资本开支的上调幅度有所放缓，表明AI投资周期的峰值正愈发清晰地进入视野。 在AI对就业市场的影响方面，高盛已观察到早期信号：在非制造业行业中，AI在常规业务功能中的采用率与就业增长之间呈现出统计显著的负相关，与失业率则呈正相关——而这一相关性在年初时尚不显著。高盛基线预测认为，AI对劳动力市场的冲击将主要集中在2028至2029年，但若经济出现下行，企业可能更激进地削减招聘目标，加速这一进程。 通胀：进展可期，但上行风险犹存 2026年通胀超预期，主要源于伊朗战争引发的能源价格上涨，全球整体通胀以四季度同比计算收于3.7%，较高盛此前预测高出1.3个百分点。 展望2027年，高盛认为通胀回落的条件正在形成。在美国，关税传导效应（目前仍为核心PCE同比增速贡献约40个基点）预计将于明年春季完全退出同比统计，叠加伊朗战争通胀冲击的消退，高盛预测美国核心PCE涨幅将从2026年底的3.2%放缓至2027年底的2.4%。 然而，通胀在2027年初仍可能保持一定黏性。高盛列举三点原因： 能源价格上涨的传导效应将延续至明年，欧洲尤为明显，例如欧洲航空票价尚未充分反映燃油成本上升； 全球内存价格预测在上一财报季再度上调，将为核心通胀提供额外推升，美国受影响尤甚； 上游成本压力有所上升和扩散，历史规律显示这将使通胀超预期风险在明年春季前保持偏高。 高盛同时指出，若伊朗局势再度升级，按其大宗商品团队的不利情景测算，2027年整体通胀将较基线高出0.9个百分点，核心通胀高出0.2个百分点。 货币政策：加息接近尾声，降息路径渐趋清晰 高盛预计美联储将在12月和明年3月各加息一次，随后于2027年12月启动降息，并在2028年再降息三次，终端利率为3.25%至3.5%。高盛认为美国利率风险偏向鸽派，原因在于美国通胀驱动因素更明显具有临时性，且美国对AI周期下行的敞口最大。 欧洲央行方面，高盛预计将于12月完成最后一次加息，随后于2027年第四季度开始正常化降息，终端利率为2.25%。英国央行预计将于明年2月最后加息至4.25%，此后维持不变，降息至3.25%终端利率的时间推迟至2028年。高盛对欧洲央行和英国央行的预测均较市场定价更为鸽派。 日本是主要例外。高盛预计日本央行将于12月货币政策会议再度加息25个基点，并在明年3月和6月继续加息，终端利率达2.0%，理由是通胀上行风险以及全球高利率对日元的压力。 在新兴市场，高盛整体持鸽派立场，预计中东欧、中东、非洲及拉丁美洲大多数央行将在2027年降息，亚洲利率则大体持平或小幅上升。 市场展望：正回报可期，但波动风险增加 高盛基线预测显示，2027年股票和债券均将录得正回报，大宗商品回报接近零。但高盛同时警告，市场面临的挑战将比宏观经济本身更为严峻。 对于股市，高盛预计标普500指数盈利增速将从2026年的36%降至2027年的11%，仍属稳健，但增速放缓意味着市场对AI投资周期见顶的担忧将逐步升温。 高盛指出，AI投资热潮对企业盈利和市值的贡献远大于对GDP增长的贡献——标普500盈利占GDP比例已创历史新高——一旦投资冲击消退，市场将面临这一高盈利份额能否持续的拷问。区域配置上，高盛建议超配美国和日本，中性配置日本以外亚洲地区及新兴市场，低配欧洲。 对于信用市场，高盛预计2027年信用利差将进一步走阔，美国高收益债将跑输，弱资质借款人尾部风险可能引发更大范围的融资市场动荡。 对于债市，高盛认为实际收益率处于近30年高位，债券的对冲价值正在逐步恢复。随着2027年下半年增长风险上升、央行加息周期接近尾声，债券与股票的负相关性有望重新显现。高盛预测美国10年期国债收益率将于2027年底降至4.6%。 对汇市，高盛基线预测为美元温和走弱，人民币在贸易顺差支撑下继续升值。若市场对美国科技股"例外论"的质疑加速，美元可能出现更大幅度的下跌，日元则将因避险需求而显著升值。 在大宗商品方面，高盛建议将其作为投资组合对冲工具，欧洲天然气期货及TTF看涨期权可作为能源价格上行风险的非对称对冲手段。此外，高盛认为随着市场周期趋于成熟，股票指数波动率更可能上升而非下降，建议投资者考虑通过虚值看跌期权或以长期看涨期权替代股票持仓来寻求更深层次的保护。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 贝森特与美联储高官交锋：通胀源于能源冲击还是需求过热，美联储加息路径争论升温
articles.summary: 美国财政部长与芝加哥联储主席就当前通胀根源公开交锋，折射出华盛顿与美联储之间日益加深的政策分歧，并为美联储12月议息会议蒙上更多不确定性。 美财政部长Scott Bessent（贝森特） 周五接受CNBC采访时呼吁美联储不应因伊朗战争引发的"能源供应冲击"而激进加息。 芝加哥联储主席Austan Goolsbee（古尔斯比） 随即在同一节目中予以回应，指出通胀已蔓延至服务业、医疗等与油价关联度低的领域，并受到AI数据中心建设带动的强劲需求推升，远非能源价格上涨所能解释。 Goolsbee明确表示，美联储"还有大量工作要做"以重建政策公信力。 近期强于预期的就业与通胀数据进一步强化了美联储继续加息的理由，部分官员甚至开始讨论在12月8日至9日的会议上采取超常规的50个基点加息幅度。 贝森特：能源冲击驱动通胀，Fed不应贸然逆转 Bessent在CNBC采访中将当前通胀归因于伊朗战争引发的油价上涨，并对美联储的政策立场提出批评。 他表示，美国整体经济基本面依然强劲，当前的通胀数据本质上是"噪音"，美联储不应以此为由大幅加息。 "美联储本应着眼未来，而非盯着后视镜，"Bessent说。他还提及美联储去年的降息举措，认为在能源供应冲击下急剧逆转政策方向"并不是我在美联储时会做的事"。 他同时表示，自己并非要直接干预美联储决策，而是希望其"保持开放心态"。 这一表态与特朗普政府的整体口径一致——政府官员普遍强调通胀的油价驱动属性，对美联储的应对方式持批评立场。 古尔斯比：通胀已超出能源范畴，更令人担忧 Goolsbee对财政部长的判断表示尊重，但明确提出了不同看法。 他指出，通胀的持续性和广泛性已超出能源和关税冲击所能解释的范围——服务业通胀、医疗费用上涨，以及AI数据中心建设带动的需求过热，均成为推高物价的独立因素。 "关税通胀和油价冲击本应在现在消退，但它们并没有，"Goolsbee说，"如果需求过热并正在助推通胀，那才是更令人担忧的情况。"他强调，服务业通胀"无论油价如何变化都不会消失"。 在通胀回归2%目标的问题上，Goolsbee直言："我目前的判断是，我们尚未走在正确的轨道上，必须正视这一现实。"他表示，即将发布的通胀数据将是判断美联储是否需要加快加息节奏的关键依据。 研究显示油价与通胀的关系更为复杂 尽管特朗普政府将通胀主要归咎于油价，但据路透报道，相关研究正在揭示油价对美国经济影响的另一面。 由于美国已成为能源净出口国，全球油价上涨不仅带来供给侧成本压力，还会通过企业利润提升和工资增长等渠道向经济体内部传导，形成独立于供应因素之外的需求侧通胀动力。 这意味着，美联储难以像处理纯粹的供给冲击那样，简单地"穿越"当前通胀。 美联储官员在伊朗战争初期曾考虑对供给驱动的通胀采取观望态度，但随着通胀持续高于目标，支持加息的立场逐渐占据上风。 12月会议前景：加息力度争议升温 近期数据正在推动市场对更激进加息路径的预期。强于预期的就业和通胀报告令部分美联储官员开始讨论在12月8日至9日会议上加息50个基点的可能性，而非通常的25个基点。 Goolsbee虽未明确承诺加息，但措辞显示政策立场趋紧。"我们已连续数月看到通胀广泛化的不良信号，"他说，"在与油价和关税无关的类别中，进展依然停滞，部分甚至在恶化。" 此番政府官员与美联储之间的公开分歧，将使外界对美联储政策独立性的关注度持续提升，12月议息会议前的通胀及就业数据走势，料将成为市场聚焦的核心变量。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 英伟达物色新CEO，接触Arm CEO Rene Haas，其曾是黄仁勋门生
articles.summary: 英伟达董事会在创始人黄仁勋因婚外情丑闻辞职后，启动了一场关乎这家4万亿美元市值AI芯片巨头命运的接班人搜寻。 11月13日，据英国《金融时报》报道， 英伟达董事会已就继任事宜接触Arm Holdings首席执行官Rene Haas。 （Arm首席执行官Rene Haas，图源：Arm官网） 这一消息提振了市场情绪，Arm美股盘中跌幅有所收窄，但仍下跌4.8%；英伟达股价同日下跌逾2%。 英伟达董事会在声明中表示，正"遴选猎头公司"，尚未"正式接触"任何候选人，并称一切有关候选人的猜测"为时尚早"。 黄仁勋于周四宣布辞职，结束了长达33年的执掌生涯。其离任导火索是外界披露他曾与至少一名下属以及一名客户存在婚外情关系。 英伟达首席财务官Colette Kress目前以代理首席执行官身份主持日常工作，英伟达董事会同步委托前联邦检察官对黄仁勋的行为展开独立调查。美国国会议员也宣布将启动独立调查。 Haas与英伟达渊源深厚 Haas在英伟达工作约七年，曾晋升为计算产品业务副总裁兼总经理，是黄仁勋亲自提携的门生，二人至今仍保持密切关系。 2013年，Haas加入Arm；2022年出任Arm首席执行官，并于次年主导完成公司在纳斯达克的上市。 Arm由软银持有，其处理器架构授权广泛应用于全球大多数智能手机芯片，同时也是英伟达AI硬件的底层技术基础。 今年，Arm推出了自研完整AI芯片，使其与自身客户形成直接竞争。此外，Haas与软银创始人孙正义关系密切，今年4月，他还被任命负责软银国际业务，协助后者构建其AI版图。 据报道，Haas目前是多位候选人之一，并无保证他将获得邀约或予以接受。 候选名单浮现 在内部候选人中 ，Colette Kress被分析师视为稳健的财务管理者；资深工程师Ian Buck则因主导开发了驱动英伟达AI芯片的软件平台CUDA而备受关注，被视为技术路线延续的核心人选。Ian Buck目前担任英伟达数据中心业务负责人。 在外部候选人方面 ，据《金融时报》援引知情人士称，AMD首席执行官苏姿丰因其在中国市场的丰富经验而受到分析人士关注；美光科技首席执行官Sanjay Mehrotra的名字也出现在讨论中，其存储芯片广泛应用于英伟达服务器。 此外据报道，Marvell首席执行官Matt Murphy以及苹果公司硬件主管Johny Srouji同样被纳入视野。特朗普此前也公开提及前苹果首席执行官库克。 领导层更迭面临多重挑战 黄仁勋在英伟达执掌33年，以高度亲力亲为著称，亲自参与工程路线制定、美国出口的地缘政治谈判，并在AI生态系统中主导了大规模投资布局。 分析师预计，下一任首席执行官将面临向更具机构化管理风格转型的压力。 与此同时，英伟达还需应对日益加强的监管审查，以及美国国会寻求进一步管制出口的政策压力。如何保持英伟达在下一代AI芯片竞赛中的技术领先优势，并管理好撬动AI热潮的数十亿美元投资协议，同样是继任者无法回避的核心命题。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄金或创六月来最大单周跌幅，美联储加息押注升温施压贵金属
articles.summary: 黄金本周遭遇重挫，受通胀顽固与美联储紧缩预期升温双重打压，势将创下自六月以来最大单周跌幅。 周五现货黄金一度小幅收复部分失地，但仍难掩整周颓势。截至纽约时间周五下午4时10分，现货金报每盎司3876美元，持平于周四纽约尾盘价格，本周累计跌幅达4.78%。 此前一日，金价曾跌至13个月低点。美国消费者价格指数连续第三个月超出预期，触发市场对美联储激进加息的重新定价，美元走强、美债收益率攀升，构成黄金的双重逆风。 美联储官员本周集体释放鹰派信号。联储理事沃勒表示，若通胀持续加速，他将支持单次加息50个基点。纽约联储主席John Williams、芝加哥联储主席Austan Goolsbee及波士顿联储主席Susan Collins亦相继呼吁采取进一步行动遏制通胀。 加息预期重新定价，黄金承压明显 消费者价格数据连续第三个月超预期，促使交易员显著上调对美联储2027年进一步加息的押注，并于本周二开始将12月单次加息50个基点的可能性纳入定价。 加息预期的转变推动美国国债收益率走高，美元随之走强。由于黄金不产生利息收益且以美元计价，收益率上行与美元走强均对其构成直接压制。 白银本周同步下跌，周五跌幅达2.36%，铂金下跌，钯金则小幅上涨。 尽管短期抛压明显，市场机构对黄金的长期前景判断趋于分化 。道明证券高级大宗商品策略师Ryan McKay指出： 宏观基金、ETF及央行等黄金多头阵营近期买入动能有限，市场因此愈发容易受到美联储加息预期重新定价的冲击。 然而，McKay同时强调，黄金的强劲支撑依然存在。他表示： 非趋势追随型投资者的整体仓位尚未出现明显平仓迹象，价格下行或将再度吸引这类仍以长期货币贬值与去美元化为主题的投资者入场布局。 从市场结构看，短期内能源价格驱动的通胀走向及美联储官员表态，将继续主导黄金的价格走势。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 在 DeepSeek App（含网页端）的对话服务中，联网搜索、文件输入、阅读链接、语音交互及安全等能力与模型推理相互配合，构成了用户熟悉的对话体验。而开发者如果想要在应用中实现类似功能，除接入原有 DeepSeek API 外，往往还需耗费大量精力去对接外部工具、处理调用衔接。 今天，我们正式开放这套全家桶应用 API：在原有 API 中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能；语音及相关底层能力也已开放独立接口（含 OCR、ASR、TTS 等），支持单独或组合调用。开发者可以在自己的应用中轻松实现复杂的对话功能，甚至 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App。 全面开放应用功能，支持独立调用 本次更新将 DeepSeek App 的各项交互功能直接整合进原有 API。开启对应参数后，相关工具调用与上下文拼接均由服务端自动完成。目前，V4.1-Flash 模型（deepseek-flash）已在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 接口下支持以下能力： 联网搜索：在非思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可根据提问自动发起网页或图片搜索并附引用作答； 深度思考搜索：在思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可在多步推理中自主联网搜索与阅读链接； 文件输入：支持上传 PDF、Office、图片等格式的文件，完成纯文本提取或图文混排解析后，拼入对话上下文供模型作答； 阅读链接：将 deepseek_read_url 工具打开后，模型可自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答； 模型安全：开启安全校验参数后，我们将提供基础风控，审核模型输入输出，命中风险时返回拒答标识。如您对外提供应用服务，请务必开启该参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记、AI 标识等义务。 此外，为方便开发者更灵活地接入自有工作流，上述底层能力及语音能力 均支持作为独立接口单独调用 ，包括：Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS。 使用上述接口，开发者即可实现与 DeepSeek App 基本一致的功能。为直观演示这一效果，我们基于新版 API 构建并开源了一份轻量的前端 Demo，支持直接导入 DeepSeek 历史对话。 Demo 体验入口：https://cdn.deepseek.com/chat-demo 示例代码入口：https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo 更详细的参数定义与调用说明，请参考 DeepSeek 官方 API 文档 [API 指南 - 构建 Chatbot]。 API 定价说明 用户调用 DeepSeek API 使用扩展能力时，除收取 Token 费用外，也将收取相关工具的调用费用。各项工具价格如下表所示： 写在后面的话 我们相信，人与模型的交互依然充满无限可能，而 DeepSeek 现有的对话产品只是较为基础的一种形态。 现在，官方产品背后的各项能力均已支持通过 DeepSeek API 随心调用、自由组合，我们期待开发者能够借此省去重复的基础工作，打造出更多样、更极致、更具想象力的产品。 欢迎使用 DeepSeek API，尽情创造。 本文来源： DeepSeek 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
